tests.name: Cross-dimensional relationship beats dimension deviation
inputs: thought partnership already shown in Section 3
tests.reason: The higher-order relationship remains eligible even though one component dimension appeared earlier; the standalone dimension claim is rejected.

tests.name: Perception gap beats repeated recognition profile
tests.reason: The perception gap is new and personally surprising; Section 1's integration claim cannot be repeated.

tests.name: Rare wording requires prevalence support
tests.reason: The engine may describe a contrast but must not use uncommon or rare wording without approved joint-prevalence evidence.

tests.name: Section 2 exact response is rejected
inputs: low verification card displayed in Section 2
tests.reason: The higher-order trust–verification relationship is allowed; repeating the low-verification card alone is not.

tests.name: Standalone dimension used only as fallback
tests.reason: Dimension deviation is selected only after all higher tiers fail.

tests.name: Section 1 private-social profile blocks repetition
tests.reason: The private/social contrast was already the recognition story and cannot become the Section 4 standout.

tests.name: Behaviour Context cannot promote report
tests.expected: Context contains no report, purchase, unlock or pricing language
tests.reason: Section 4 creates an unresolved question through complexity, not a sales prompt.

tests.name: Only one standout output
tests.reason: Tie-break order produces exactly one finding and no secondary card.

tests.name: Balanced profile fallback
tests.reason: The engine must not manufacture a standout when the participant's pattern is genuinely even.

tests.name: Dimension fallback clears threshold
tests.reason: A standalone dimension may win only when it clears the provisional minimum threshold.

tests.name: Dimension fallback fails threshold
tests.reason: A weak relative leader is not enough to justify standout language.
